controls.guidance: Static analysis tools (such as SAST or IaC security scanners) check source code for common vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. By running static analysis tools earlier in the DevSecOps cycle, vulnerabilities can be detected and prevented from being deployed to production.
controls.risk: Without setting up static analysis in the CI/CD pipeline for each merge request and addressing true positive vulnerability findings, there is an increased risk of deploying insecure code to the production branch, potentially leading to security breaches and compromise of the overall system.

controls.title: Dependency Scanning
controls.statement: Schedule a scan at least every [time period (days)] day(s) in the [location] to identify the use of vulnerable software libraries.
controls.guidance: Dependency scanning checks the source code for dependencies with known vulnerabilities. By running scans regularly using bots or software composition analysis (SCA) tools, vulnerabilities arising from outdated dependencies can be quickly detected and patched. Software composition analysis can be performed using tools such as Gitlab, Nexus IQ, or their equivalent, with output in a common SBOM format such as SPDX or CycloneDX.
controls.risk: Failing to schedule regular dependency scanning to identify vulnerable software libraries and address findings in a timely manner increases the risk of deploying applications with known vulnerabilities, potentially exposing the system to security exploits and compromise.

controls.title: Secret Detection
controls.statement: Set up secret detection in the [location] and remediate true positives within [time period (days)] day(s).
controls.guidance: Ensure that the exposed secret is revoked and purged from the Git history.
controls.risk: Without setting up secret detection and addressing true positive findings promptly, there's an increased risk of exposing sensitive information, potential unauthorised access, and compromised security.

controls.title: CI Environment Variable Secrets Management
controls.statement: Protect environment variable secrets used in CI jobs by limiting them to protected pipelines and masking them in job logs.
controls.guidance: Use GitLab's CI/CD variable security settings or GitHub's encrypted secrets with the add-mask workflow command.
controls.risk: Failing to protect environment variable secrets in CI jobs by limiting them to protected pipelines and masking them in job logs increases the risk of unauthorised access and exposure of sensitive information.

controls.title: Deployment Environment Segregation
controls.statement: Segregate production and non-production environments including applications, services, data, secrets, roles, and networks.
controls.guidance: Achieve segregation using separate cloud tenant accounts for environments such as production, development, test, and staging. Account segregation enhances security by limiting exposure, simplifies resource and cost management, maintains configuration integrity, facilitates compliance and auditing and streamlines operational tasks. Deploy and operate environments as similarly as possible to enhance debugging and time-to-market.
controls.risk: Failure to segregate production and non-production environments increases the risk of unauthorised access, data leaks, and denial of service attacks, as compromises in non-production environments may lead to cascading impacts on production systems.

controls.title: Separate hosting
controls.statement: Physically separate Government resources from non-Government resources.
controls.guidance: For on-premise environments, ensure government resources are physically stored and secured separately from non-government resources.
controls.risk: Violating this control can subject government data and systems to access risks leading to compromised systems and data.

controls.title: Physical Access Controls
controls.statement: Implement physical access controls to prohibit unauthorised access to the hosting environment or network rooms.
controls.guidance: Measures to consider include: a) personnel security clearance and checks b) Continuous monitoring c) Immediate security response d) Strong authentication card access system to regulate and log access of employees, visitors and contractors to the facility; e) Guards deployed to guard the facility 24/7; f) Restrict items (such as unauthorised computing devices) to be brought into the facility; g) Intrusion Detection System installed to detect unauthorised access; h) CCTV installed to monitor the facility.
controls.risk: Violating this control can subject government data and systems to access risks leading to compromised systems and data.

controls.title: Software as a Service (SaaS) Service Level Agreement
controls.statement: Obtain a service level agreement with the SaaS provider.
controls.guidance: Ensure the service level agreement covers uptime, response times, downtime notifications, support channels (such as email or phone), and security resources (access logs, incident reports, incident logs to aid in investigations, SOC 2 Type 2 report). Regularly check for compliance to the agreement.
controls.risk: Without a service level agreement the availability of the Software as a Service (SaaS) system may be poorly maintained by the provider.

controls.title: Third Party Audit
controls.statement: Conduct a(n) [type of audit] audit by an independent third-party at least every [time period (days)] day(s).
controls.guidance: The scope of the audit should cover the compliance requirements of the system owner.
controls.risk: Failure to conduct an independent third-party audit may reduce visibility of security weaknesses.

controls.title: Scope for Offshoring
controls.statement: Restrict offshore development to development and maintenance work.
controls.guidance: Organisation can only offshore development and maintenance works in non-production environment to third party.
controls.risk: Offshoring systems increases risks such as cybersecurity threats, data breaches, quality issues, and operational disruptions. Therefore, only systems with a lower risk profile should be considered for offshoring.

controls.title: Attestation Report Review
controls.statement: Review the [audit] attestation report every [time period (days)] day(s) and ensure that outstanding exceptions or findings are remediated.
controls.guidance: The scope of the attestation report should minimally cover the risk assessment, risk mitigation, logical and physical access controls, system operations and change management and should be perfomed by an independent third party.
controls.risk: Without reviewing the audit report by an independent third party may pose security and compliance risks as there is no independent verification that the system meets industry standards relating to data management and security controls, which potentially lead to data breaches and reputational damage.

controls.title: Qualified Offshore Development Centre
controls.statement: Engage offshore resources through a local third party that operates a [type].
controls.guidance: Engage offshore resources through a local third party that operates a Overseas Development Centre selected by GovTech or consult GovTech before engaging offshore resources.
controls.risk: Not engaging with local Third-Party operating a GovTech qualified ODC, or not engaging GovTech before engaging offshore resources can result in undesirable outcomes where Agencies interests are unprotected.

controls.title: Supplier Assessments and Reviews
controls.statement: Seek an assessment by [Assessing party] on the risks associated with suppliers or contractors before using or subscribing to the service.
controls.guidance: Submit SaaS usage via the Request for SaaS FormSG and the assessment outcome will be provided within 3 working days.
controls.risk: Failure to assess suppliers may introduce supply chain risks associated with data residency and jurisdiction.

controls.title: Cryptographic Key Establishment
controls.statement: Use industry-standard cryptographic key establishment schemes and key derivation methods.
controls.guidance: Refer to SP 800-56A, SP 800-56B, and SP 800-56C for updated industry-standard cryptographic key establishment schemes and key derivation methods. Cloud services such as AWS Key Management Service and Azure Key Vault can be used for generating and managing cryptographic keys.
controls.risk: Insecure cryptographic key establishment can lead to weak or broken encryption.

controls.title: Cryptographic Key Rotation
controls.statement: Rotate cryptographic keys every [time period (days)] days.
controls.guidance: Cloud services such as AWS Key Management Service and Azure Key Vault enable automatic rotation of cryptographic keys.
controls.risk: Failing to rotate cryptographic keys increases the risk of broken encryption.

controls.title: Cryptographic Key Management
controls.statement: Implement cryptographic key management processes to ensure cryptographic keys are well-managed and safeguarded throughout their lifecycle.
controls.guidance: Follow key management practices such as those described in NIST SP 800-57 or ISO/IEC 27017 to cover aspects including generation, registration, storage, distribution, installation, use, rotation, backup, recovery, revocation, suspension, and destruction of keys.
controls.risk: Inadequate key management increase the risk of unauthorised access, data breaches, and compromised cryptographic operations due to poorly managed or safeguarded cryptographic keys.
